COMM 211 FINAL

What’s the Issue?
●
Target’s marketing is geared toward younger, 
digital-ﬁrst shoppers.
●
Older consumers (ages 30–50) feel disconnected 
from the brand.
●
This demographic prefers:
○
In-store shopping
○
Quality-focused purchases
○
Brand familiarity and consistency
●
As Target pushes online convenience, it’s losing 
relevance with this key group.
Problem
COMM 211 FINAL

Why It Matters
●
Older shoppers are high-spending, loyal, and 
family-oriented.
●
They often shop at multiple stores because they 
perceive Target as “convenient,” not “high-quality.”
●
Recent PR issues have damaged brand trust, 
especially among older professionals.
Result:
Target risks long-term loyalty and sales from a major 
demographic.
Problem
COMM 211 FINAL

Situation Analysis
Company Overview
●
Mission: "Help all families discover the joy of everyday life"
●
Brand Promise: "Expect More. Pay Less."
●
Founded: 1902 (as Dayton Dry Goods); Target brand launched 1962
●
Scale: 1,989 U.S. stores, $106.57B revenue, 440,000 employees
●
Iconic mascot: Bullseye Dog (introduced 1999)
Market Position
●
Positioning: Higher quality than Walmart, more affordable than specialty retailers
●
Key Competitors: Walmart, Amazon, Costco, Kohl's, Home Depot
●
Differentiation: Trendy exclusive brands, designer collaborations, elevated shopping 
experience
●
Geographic Reach: 75% of U.S. within 10 miles of a Target store

Marketing & Advertising 
Objectives
●
Rebuild Emotional Connection with Older 
Consumers
○
“Bullseye the Dog” - nostalgic feeling
○
Reintroduced in stores, social media, 
advertising
●
Improve Target’s Image as a Quality Driven and 
Family Centered Retailer
○
Redesigned in-store signage, advertising, and 
partnerships that highlight reliability and 
product quality
●
Build Global Brand Awareness Without Physical 
Expansion
○
Creative solution storyboard, media digital 
campaigns, and social media platforms 
(Facebook, YouTube, and Instagram). 
○
Emphasis on traditional brand identity 
centered on affordability, family values, and 
its slogan “Expect More. Pay Less”.

“
For families who seek quality products and meaningful shopping 
experiences, Target is the family-centered retailer that delivers both 
affordable quality and nostalgic comfort to your shopping cart. We've been 
part of your family's story for generations - from your ﬁrst memories of 
Bullseye to creating new ones with your own children - rekindling the joy of 
family shopping by bringing back the emotional connections that made us 
America's beloved shopping destination. We aim to continue proving that 
quality, value, and family moments can all happen under one roof, all while 
maintaining the "Expect More. Pay Less." promise that bridges the gap 
between premium quality with everyday affordability.

Evaluation
Why Our Campaign Works
●
“Bring Bullseye Home” reconnects older 
consumers through nostalgia and trust.
●
Reintroducing Bullseye strengthens 
familiarity and emotional appeal.
●
Telling a heartfelt story (Bullseye returning 
home) mirrors older consumers reconnecting 
with Target.
●
Consistent red-and-white visuals reinforce 
Target’s classic identity.
COMM 211 FINAL

Impact & Expected Results
●
Strong reach: 75% of Americans live within 10 miles of a 
Target.
●
Roundel + Target Circle allow precise tracking of 
engagement and sentiment.
●
Key metrics: impressions, social engagement, in-store 
visits, website traffic, brand sentiment.
●
Projected ROI: 3–5x return on digital ad spend + growth 
in loyalty among 30–50-year-olds.
